Fair working conditions - contracts that reflect actual hours worked, with a mechanism for six-monthly reviews (and/or the ability to request a review more frequently) and adjust contracts if actual hours regularly exceed contracted hours or if the employee requests a change in actual hours worked

- plans to engage the contract workforce in deciding the most important workplace issues to address and how identified issues will be acted upon, monitored, and reviewed

- provide parental, family and kinship leave such as offering paid maternity, paternity, adoption, or carer’s leave beyond the statutory minimum length of time and pay

- special or personal (or equivalent) leave provisions to support workers experiencing situational difficulties or requiring time off work, for example to allow survivors of domestic abuse to attend court hearings

- provide or develop safeguarding plans for workers who require these arrangements, including upholding existing obligations around domestic violence and third party harassment

- offer clear information to employees on flexible working arrangements, working hours, and alternative work location options, guidance on how to apply for these arrangements, and a commitment to meet these requests where possible to do so

- offer clear information to employees on workplace health and wellbeing support, occupational health provision, reasonable adjustments, and support for employees returning after illness, guidance on how to apply for these arrangements, and a commitment to meet these requests where possible to do so

Annex E: Further information on social value and value for money

PPN 026 does not replace the requirements included in other guidance documents or legislation. You should ensure that you follow the expectations set out elsewhere and where your legal obligations conflict with the PPN 026, you must meet your legal obligations.

You are also able to take into account broader social value expectations, such as carbon emissions or modern slavery as set out in other PPNs or with their own weighting in your procurements. However, this should be in addition to the 10% or 20% weighting applied to the Social Value Model and not form part of this weighting. There may also be opportunities to use the existing outcomes in ways that align with your wider organisation objectives, for example, by encouraging the creation of jobs or skills as a part of a talent pipeline in the clean energy industry if your organisation has environmental objectives and this is appropriate for your contract.

1. The Green Book

The government uses the Green Book to evaluate policies, projects, and programmes to ensure public money is spent effectively. By applying Green Book principles, decision-makers can select proposals that achieve their intended objectives while delivering improved social welfare and community benefits. For further details on how to handle public funds, refer to the Managing public money guidance.

2. Public Services (Social Value) Act 2012

When procuring services, or services together with goods and/or works, you should have regard to the Public Services (Social Value) Act 2012[footnote 21] to ensure your procurement is compliant. It requires public authorities in England and Wales (with some exceptions in Wales) to consider when procuring services;

how what is being proposed might improve the economic, social, and environmental wellbeing of the relevant area

how in conducting the process of procurement, it might act with a view to securing that improvement

whether to take and consultation on the above points

The Social Value Model is designed to align with the Public Services (Social Value) Act 2012, however, as part of your business case process and before the procurement begins, you should ensure that you have given due regard to the Act.

3. The National Procurement Policy Statement

The Procurement Act 2023 sets out that contracting authorities must have regard to the National Procurement Policy Statement (NPPS) when procuring public contracts, unless they are exempted. The NPPS sets the government’s strategic priorities for public procurement in support of the government’s missions whilst still achieving value for money and social value.

4. Researching local communities

This table includes examples of sources you can use to research the needs of local communities and cohorts, but you should use other resources relevant to specific communities, regions, and industries to assess the market if needed.

passages.quote:
1. Introduction

1.1. Definition

The government wants taxpayers’ money to be spent in a way that values and invests in local communities. For in-scope central government contracting authorities, social value through procurement using the Social Value Model is defined as:

‘taking account of how a supplier will work for our communities to provide good British jobs, skills and opportunities in every postcode’

1.2. Who is this guidance for?

This guidance is for commercial practitioners procuring contracts in scope of Procurement Policy Note 026 (PPN 026). It explains how to use PPN 026: The Social Value Model in all stages of the procurement process.

PPN 026 replaces all previous PPNs on social value. From 1 January 2027, you should apply PPN 026 to new covered procurements worth £1m or more. If you award a contract using a framework set up before this date, you may need to consider the PPN in use at the time the framework was awarded. For frameworks procured:

before 1 January 2027 but on or after 24 February 2025, use PPN 002 [footnote 1]

before 24 February 2025 but on or after 1 January 2021, use PPN 06/20 [footnote 2]

If using previous models, you should still select outcomes that deliver jobs, skills, and opportunities. See section 4.3 for details on awarding contracts using frameworks.

You should apply the correct Social Value Model weighting and publish Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) as needed, depending on contract value. You do not need to apply PPN 026 if a modification changes the value of the contract.

Please contact info@gca.gov.uk if you have any questions.

1.2. Wider obligations and value for money

You should apply this guidance in compliance with legal requirements and international obligations. Departing from this guidance is permitted when necessary to comply with international agreements, and to keep requirements relevant and proportionate and ensure fair treatment and non-discrimination.

See Annex E for more information on social value in the context of value for money, and how PPN 026 aligns with other procurement policies including the Green Book and National Procurement Policy Statement (NPPS).

1.3. The Social Value Model award criteria

PPN 026 sets out the government’s social value priorities for procurement. It provides model award criteria for you to choose from. See Annex B for the full Model, including sub-criteria, standard reporting metrics, and the target cohorts.

Outcome Social Value Model award criteria

Good Jobs 1a. Create high-quality jobs

Good Jobs 1b. Fair working conditions

Good Jobs 1c. Fair pay

Skills 2a. Training / Retraining

Skills 2b. In-work progression

Skills 2c. Talent Pipeline

1.4. Actions to take

This guidance covers the four stages of the commercial lifecycle and corresponding actions.

Stage Actions

Plan 1. Build awareness within your organisation of using the Social Value Model to deliver jobs, skills and opportunities.

Plan 2. Identify your procurement pipeline and engage with stakeholders to determine the social value outcomes your contracts can deliver.

Define 1. Assess the market and determine the market maturity for successfully delivering Social Value Model outcomes.

Define 2. Identify achievable Social Value Model outcomes, criteria, and sub-criteria that align with your organisation’s objectives and your legal duties, and are additional to the core purpose of the contract.

Define 3. Set an effective scoring methodology to evaluate social value in suppliers’ tenders. See Annex C for an example methodology.

Define 4. Test your selected policy outcomes, criteria, sub-criteria, metrics and scoring methodology during preliminary market engagement.

Define 5. Where relevant, eEncourage suppliers to build relationships with relevant Community Programmes during preliminary market engagement.

Procure 1. Complete the Social Value Model question by including relevant target cohorts, award criteria, and sub-criteria for your selected Social Value Model outcome(s) in your procurement documents.

Procure 2. If appropriate, include the List of Community Programmes, removing any sections that are not relevant to your contract.

Procure 3. Evaluate the quality of supplier tenders against the Social Value Model award criteria and sub-criteria published in your tender documentation.

Procure 4. Notify successful and unsuccessful suppliers and send assessment summaries that include details of your evaluation.

Procure 5. Agree the Key Performance Indicator or performance indicator, with the supplier for the social value commitments they made.

Procure 6. Document the social value commitments in your contract.

Manage 1. Manage the social value deliverables against the supplier’s commitments set out in your contract.

Manage 2. Publish a contract performance notice at least once every 12 months for contracts worth £5m or more, detailing supplier performance against your agreed metrics.

Manage 3. Government departments should submit quarterly social value reports to the Cabinet Office reporting all social value commitments using the standard reporting metrics.

2. Plan

In the ‘Plan’ stage you will prepare to select the most appropriate outcomes and Social Value Model award criteria to achieve the government’s social value priorities.

2.1. Build awareness

You should share this guidance with colleagues outside your commercial function to raise awareness and familiarity with the Social Value Model and how it supports local communities and the government’s priorities. You can use this guidance to develop an effective commercial strategy that sets clear objectives that align the government’s social value priorities set out in PPN 026 with your organisation’s goals.
